ikd.title: Inherited kidney disease
ikd.description: Structured history and findings for an inherited kidney disease assessment.
ikd.limitations: These 42 questions across eight disease profiles are an incomplete research assessment. Three shared family-history prompts record patterns that may suggest dominant, recessive, or X-linked inheritance; they do not establish a genetic diagnosis. Unticked findings are recorded as absent for this proof of concept. Family-history prompts have zero score weight while the other present findings add candidate weights derived from LIRICAL. Scores are not calibrated disease probabilities or diagnostic criteria. A zero score does not exclude disease. A negative or unclear family history does not exclude disease, and Alport remains a broad profile without inheritance subtypes. Related findings may inflate totals, profiles have different selected features, and UMOD and MUC1 remain hard to distinguish. Timing of gout is not encoded.
ikd.associationContext: This is background context; an answer here does not establish or exclude a diagnosis.

questions.label: Documented family history suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance
questions.question: Does the documented family history show a similar condition in successive generations?
questions.help: A pattern in a parent and child or across successive generations may suggest dominant inheritance. A negative or unclear family history does not exclude disease.

questions.label: Documented family history suggesting autosomal recessive inheritance
questions.question: Does the documented family history show affected siblings with unaffected parents?
questions.help: Affected siblings with unaffected parents may suggest recessive inheritance. An isolated case or no affected siblings does not exclude it.

questions.label: Documented family history suggesting X-linked inheritance
questions.question: Does transmission among affected relatives in the documented family history suggest an X-linked pattern?
questions.help: Affected relatives through the maternal line or affected daughters of an affected father may suggest X-linked inheritance. There is no father-to-son transmission. Females can also be affected, and an unclear pedigree does not exclude it.

questions.label: Decreased glomerular filtration rate
questions.question: Has a decreased glomerular filtration rate been documented?
questions.help: Records documented reduced GFR without inferring chronicity, cause or a new laboratory threshold.

questions.label: Enlarged kidney
questions.question: Has kidney enlargement been documented on imaging?
questions.help: Records documented kidney enlargement without applying a size threshold.

questions.label: Glomerular basement membrane lamellation
questions.question: Has glomerular basement membrane lamellation been documented in a kidney biopsy report?
questions.help: Requires the named biopsy finding. an unspecified abnormal biopsy is insufficient.

questions.label: Horseshoe kidney
questions.question: Has a horseshoe kidney been documented on imaging?
questions.help: Records the named structural kidney finding.

imageGuidance.description: No reference image selected: this finding does not need a visual recognition aid in Atlas.

questions.label: Hyperechogenic kidneys
questions.question: Have hyperechogenic kidneys been documented on ultrasound?
questions.help: Records increased renal echogenicity in the ultrasound report. This is nonspecific and does not establish a genetic diagnosis.

imageGuidance.description: No reference image selected: this finding does not need a visual recognition aid in Atlas.

questions.label: Microscopic haematuria
questions.question: Has microscopic haematuria been documented on urine testing?
questions.help: Specifically documented microscopic haematuria.

questions.label: Multicystic kidney dysplasia
questions.question: Has multicystic kidney dysplasia been documented?
questions.help: Records explicitly documented dysplasia. renal cysts alone do not establish this finding.

questions.label: Multiple renal cysts
questions.question: Have multiple renal cysts been documented on imaging?
questions.help: Multiple renal cysts explicitly documented in an imaging report.

questions.label: Polycystic kidney dysplasia
questions.question: Has polycystic kidney dysplasia been documented?
questions.help: Requires the named structural finding. multiple renal cysts alone are insufficient.

questions.label: Proteinuria
questions.question: Has proteinuria been documented?
questions.help: Records documented protein in the urine without applying a quantitative threshold.

questions.label: Renal agenesis
questions.question: Has renal agenesis been documented?
questions.help: Records congenital absence of a kidney. an acquired solitary kidney is not equivalent.

questions.label: Renal angiomyolipoma
questions.question: Has a renal angiomyolipoma been documented on imaging?
questions.help: Records a documented kidney lesion, without applying a size or number threshold.

referenceImage.alt: Side-by-side axial kidney CT images before and after contrast, with an arrow pointing to a renal angiomyolipoma.
referenceImage.caption: Example renal angiomyolipoma on CT before (left) and after (right) contrast. This image is an example, not a diagnostic template.
referenceImage.credit: Greco et al., Journal of Renal and Hepatic Disorders (2018)

questions.label: Renal cell carcinoma
questions.question: Has renal cell carcinoma been documented?
questions.help: A documented renal cell carcinoma diagnosis.

questions.label: Renal corticomedullary cysts
questions.question: Have renal corticomedullary cysts been documented on imaging?
questions.help: Requires documented corticomedullary location. Simple cysts elsewhere are not equivalent. Cysts may be absent in ADTKD.

imageGuidance.description: No reference image selected: this finding does not need a visual recognition aid in Atlas.

questions.label: Renal tubular atrophy
questions.question: Has renal tubular atrophy been documented on a previous kidney biopsy?
questions.help: Use an existing histopathology report. This assessment does not recommend obtaining a biopsy.

imageGuidance.description: No reference image selected: this finding does not need a visual recognition aid in Atlas.

questions.label: Angiofibromas
questions.question: Have angiofibromas been identified?
questions.help: Records the broad angiofibroma finding, without restricting it to facial lesions or applying a count.

referenceImage.alt: Clinical photograph of multiple raised papules over the nose, cheeks and forehead, with the eyes masked in the source image.
referenceImage.caption: Facial angiofibromas in a published tuberous sclerosis example. Appearance varies between individuals.
referenceImage.credit: M. Sand, D. Sand, C. Thrandorf, V. Paech, P. Altmeyer and F. G. Bechara (2010). Unmodified source image.

imageGuidance.description: Facial angiofibromas in a published tuberous sclerosis example. Appearance varies between individuals.

questions.label: Angiokeratomas
questions.question: Have angiokeratomas been identified?
questions.help: Records whether these vascular skin lesions have been identified.

referenceImage.alt: Two clinical photographs showing red-purple angiokeratomas near the navel and on the oral mucosa.
referenceImage.caption: Examples of Fabry-associated angiokeratomas near the navel and on the oral mucosa.

questions.label: Hypomelanotic macules
questions.question: Have hypomelanotic macules been identified?
questions.help: Records identified patches of skin with reduced pigmentation. No lesion count is applied.

referenceImage.alt: Three-panel clinical image. the top panel shows pale hypomelanotic macules on the trunk and arms.
referenceImage.caption: Top panel (A): hypomelanotic macules. The other panels show different TSC skin findings.
referenceImage.credit: Portocarrero et al., Anais Brasileiros de Dermatologia (2018)

questions.label: Reduced sweating
questions.question: Does the patient report reduced sweating?
questions.help: Records a history of sweating less than expected.

questions.label: Shagreen patch
questions.question: Has a shagreen patch been identified?
questions.help: Records whether this skin finding has been identified.

referenceImage.alt: Three-panel clinical image. the middle panel shows a textured shagreen patch on the lower back.
referenceImage.caption: Middle panel (B): shagreen patch. The other panels show different TSC skin findings.
referenceImage.credit: Portocarrero et al., Anais Brasileiros de Dermatologia (2018)

questions.label: Anterior lenticonus
questions.question: Has anterior lenticonus been documented on eye examination?
questions.help: Records a documented lens finding. the patient is not asked to identify it.

questions.label: Cornea verticillata
questions.question: Has cornea verticillata been documented on eye examination?
questions.help: Records a documented corneal finding. It does not ask the patient to identify it.

referenceImage.alt: Slit-lamp photograph showing a faint whorl pattern in the cornea of a patient with Fabry disease.
referenceImage.caption: Cornea verticillata seen on slit-lamp examination in Fabry disease.

questions.label: Retinal capillary haemangioma
questions.question: Has a retinal capillary haemangioma been documented?
questions.help: Records the specific documented retinal lesion. other retinal lesions are not equivalent.

questions.label: Retinal flecks
questions.question: Have retinal flecks been documented on eye examination?
questions.help: Records the named retinal finding without inferring an inherited cause.

questions.label: Acroparaesthesia
questions.question: Has the patient experienced episodes of burning or tingling pain in the hands or feet?
questions.help: Episodes of pain or abnormal sensation in the extremities.

questions.label: Cerebellar haemangioblastoma
questions.question: Has a cerebellar haemangioblastoma been documented?
questions.help: Records the named tumour and location, not an unspecified brain lesion.

questions.label: Seizures
questions.question: Is there a history of seizures?
questions.help: Records a history of seizures without implying when they occurred.

questions.label: Bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment
questions.question: Has sensorineural hearing impairment in both ears been documented?
questions.help: Documented sensorineural impairment affecting both ears.

questions.label: Endolymphatic sac tumour
questions.question: Has an endolymphatic sac tumour been documented?
questions.help: Records the named tumour. hearing impairment alone is insufficient.

questions.label: Adrenal pheochromocytoma
questions.question: Has an adrenal pheochromocytoma been documented?
questions.help: Requires the documented tumour diagnosis. hypertension alone does not establish this finding.

questions.label: Diabetes mellitus
questions.question: Has diabetes mellitus been documented?
questions.help: Records documented diabetes without inferring its type, genetic cause or age at onset.

questions.label: Gout
questions.question: Has gout been clinically documented?
questions.help: Records diagnosed gout, not hyperuricaemia alone. This question does not encode whether gout preceded kidney impairment.

questions.label: Hyperuricaemia
questions.question: Has hyperuricaemia been documented?
questions.help: Records a documented elevated urate finding without applying a new laboratory threshold.

questions.label: Pancreatic aplasia or hypoplasia
questions.question: Has pancreatic aplasia or hypoplasia been documented?
questions.help: Records documented absent or underdeveloped pancreatic tissue. diabetes alone is insufficient.

questions.label: Pancreatic endocrine tumour
questions.question: Has a pancreatic endocrine tumour been documented?
questions.help: Records the specific tumour diagnosis. an unspecified pancreatic lesion is insufficient.

questions.label: Congenital hepatic fibrosis
questions.question: Has congenital hepatic fibrosis been documented?
questions.help: Records congenital hepatic fibrosis. unspecified liver fibrosis does not establish this subtype.

questions.label: Oligohydramnios in the patient’s prenatal history
questions.question: Was oligohydramnios documented during the pregnancy in which this patient was carried?
questions.help: Refers to the patient’s own prenatal history, not a later pregnancy carried by the patient. Unknown if records are unavailable.

questions.label: Portal hypertension
questions.question: Has portal hypertension been documented?
questions.help: Records documented portal hypertension, separately from systemic arterial hypertension.

questions.label: Hypertension
questions.question: Has hypertension been documented?
questions.help: Documented hypertension without deriving a diagnosis from a single blood pressure.
